\begin{frame}{Chapter 2: Sets}

\begin{itemize}
\item Basic set operations
\end{itemize}
\ex{2}{}{Let $A=\{a,b,c,d\}$, $B=\{c,d,e,f\}$, $C=\{e,f,g\}$,
and $U=\{a,b,c,d,e,f,g,\}$.
\begin{itemize}
\item Find $A\cup B$
\item Find $A\cap B$
\item Find $A\cap C$
\item Find $A'$
\item Find $(A\cup B)'$
\item Find $A'\cap B'$
\item Find $n(A)$
\item Find $n(A\cup B)$
\end{itemize}
}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Chapter 2: Sets}

\begin{itemize}
\item Venn Diagrams
\end{itemize}
\ex{2}{}{A class has $50$ students. $20$ are biology majors, $30$
are math majors, and $10$ are math and biology majors. Construct
and Venn diagram and label the number of students in each region}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Chapter 2: Counting}

\begin{itemize}
\item Basic operations:
\end{itemize}
\ex{2}{}{Find the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item $5!$
\item $\dfrac{100!}{98!}$
\item $_{5}P_{3}$
\item $_{5}C_{3}$
\end{itemize}
}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Chapter 2: Counting }

\begin{columns}


\column{3.75cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item []\textbf{Fundamental Principle of Counting:}
\item <2->When things can be repeated.
\item []\ex{3}{}{A multiple choice test has 3 options for problems 1-3
and 4 options for problem 4-5. How many different ways can you select
answers?}\vfill
\end{itemize}

\column{3.75cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item []\textbf{Permutations:}
\item <4->No repeats
\item <5->Order matters
\item <6->$_{n}P_{k}=\dfrac{n!}{(n-k)!}$
\item []\ex{7}{}{How many ways can we choose \nth{1}, \nth{2}, and \nth{3}
place in a beauty contest with 5 contestants?}\vfill
\end{itemize}

\column{3.75cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item []\textbf{Combinations:}
\item <8->No repeats
\item <9->Order does not matter
\item <10->$_{n}C_{k}=\dfrac{n!}{(n-k)!k!}$
\item []\ex{11}{11}{How many ways can we choose 3 out of 5 contestants?}\vfill
\item []\ex{12}{}{There are 10 balls. 6 blue and 4 red. Four balls are
randomly selected. Find the probability that at least 2 are blue.}\vfill
\end{itemize}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Chapter 3: Probability}

\begin{columns}


\column{5.5cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item []\textbf{Find Simple Probability}
\item <2->$P(A)=\dfrac{n(A)}{n(U)}$
\item []\ex{3}{}{What is the probability that a $Q\spadesuit$ is drawn
from a 52 card deck}
\end{itemize}

\column{4cm}
\begin{itemize}
\item []\textbf{Sample Space:}
\item <4->List of everything that can happen
\item []\ex{5}{}{Two children are born; each is a girl or boy. Find the
sample space}
\item []\ex{6}{}{What is the probability of having a boy and a girl?}
\end{itemize}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Chapter 3: Probability}

\begin{itemize}
\item []\textbf{With Venn Diagrams}
\end{itemize}
\ex{2}{}{A candy bag has $25\%$ caramels, $40\%$ chocolates, and
$15\%$ chocolate caramels. If you randomly grab a candy, find the
probability of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item [a.]It is a caramel or a chocolate.
\item [b.]It is neither a caramel or chocolate candy.
\item [c.]It is just a chocolate candy.
\end{itemize}
}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Chapter 3: Probability}

\textbf{Conditional Probability}
\begin{columns}


\column{5.5cm}

\textbf{From a chart}
\begin{itemize}
\item <2->[]\scalebox{.65}{%
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline 
\textbf{Age} & \textbf{Obama} & \textbf{McCain} & \textbf{Other/NA}\tabularnewline
\hline 
18-29 & 11.9\% & 5.8\% & 0.4\%\tabularnewline
\hline 
30-44 & 15.1\% & 13.3\% & 0.6\%\tabularnewline
\hline 
45-64 & 18.5\% & 18.1\% & 0.4\%\tabularnewline
\hline 
65+ & 7.2\% & 8.5\% & 0.3\%\tabularnewline
\hline 
\end{tabular}}
\item []\ex{3}{}{What is the prob. that a voter over 44 voted for McCain?}
\end{itemize}

\column{5.5cm}

\textbf{Using a tree diagram}

\ex{4}{}{A car lot has $60\%$ blue cars and the rest are red. Of
the blue cars $25\%$ are used and the rest are new. Of the red cars
$80\%$ are used and the rest are new.
\begin{itemize}
\item [a.]Draw a tree diagram.
\item [b.]Find the probability that a red car is new.
\item [c.]Find the probability that a randomly selected car is red AND
it is new.
\end{itemize}
}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\item <6->Find the probability that a value is below, above, or between

\item <8->Find the standard deviation such that a given probability is
